why: The new examples pushed the scorer to prefer earlier cuts on short pieces (≤3–7 words), which caused it to split predicates/negations away from their suffixes (e.g. isolating “diagnosis” from “cannot be made”) and so lowered H_set there, while the same changes encouraged merging adjacent content words and preserving enumerations in longer chunks (helping ≥10-word bins). This mixed effect produced a small net negative mean with harms concentrated in the shortest bins.
lesson: A later revision should avoid teaching a blanket leftward cut bias that isolates predicates/negations on very short pieces even if it helps merge noun compounds or enumerations in longer contexts.
